subject: Differences in output with and without data imputation

messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Differences in output with and without data imputation
parts:
Hi GGIR users,

I understand that GGIR comes with a function for data imputation (default is do.imp=TRUE). I am interested to know how different the results would be comparing to those without imputation (do.imp=FALSE). I have compared the output from part5 (both day- and person-summary) and they are pretty much the same. Does anyone know which output file should I be looking at or perhaps to share your thoughts of how different the results could be without the data imputation? Thanks!

messages.author: fe461312361bc741
messages.subject: Re: Differences in output with and without data imputation
parts:
Hi John,

I analyzed 3 of my files without imputation and got equal results. However, our participants were not supposed to take the accelerometer of at all. I suppose the difference depends on the amount of invalid data, of which in our case there should not be any.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Differences in output with and without data imputation
parts:
Hi John,
The answer to your question depends on how much invalid (non-wear) data there is. The more non-wear, the more imputation will have an influence.
Vincent
